S1_incident_reporting.quote: Manufacturers must report every thermal incident involving overheating, smoke, fire, injury, property damage, or emergency shutdown to the relevant regulator within 24 hours of learning of it, including incidents learned of after initial sale. They must provide a verified follow-up report within 10 business days. The manufacturer must notify affected customers within 48 hours when an incident presents a credible safety risk or requires customer action, and promptly update them as material information becomes available.

S2_thermal_testing.quote: Each model must undergo a sustained-heat test at 55 °C using a regulator-approved protocol and a representative sample before sale and after material design changes. The observed failure rate must not exceed 5% for any model. Before purchase, customers must be given the results for the model they are considering; existing customers must receive results for their model within 30 days of verification.

S3_remote_shutoff.quote: All new home battery units must support remote emergency shut-off, with safeguards against unauthorized activation and clear instructions for customers and emergency responders. Manufacturers must retrofit installed units that lack this capability, or provide an equally effective regulator-approved alternative, within six years after adoption.

S4_fire_suppression.quote: New home battery units must include built-in fire suppression or an independently verified equivalent protective system. This requirement takes effect 36 months after adoption.

S5_customer_disclosure.quote: Manufacturers must promptly send affected customers safety notices describing the hazard, urgency, and specific actions to take, and provide updates when instructions change. A manufacturer must initiate a recall when any model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a rolling 12-month period; the regulator must be notified promptly and customers must receive direct notice and an effective remedy.

document.section_notes: S1 is strict: all incidents must be reported within 24 hours, customers notified within 48 hours, and suspected incidents cannot be omitted pending confirmation. S2 adopts the 5% failure limit at 55°C, gives per-model results to customers and regulators without public publication, and pauses new marketing on exceedance unless a bounded regulator-approved alternative is authorized. S3 and S4 land in acceptable ranges with a six-year retrofit deadline and 36-month suppression/equivalence deadline. S5 keeps the mandatory 8/100k recall trigger but only requires prompt customer notices and lacks an explicit serious-injury clause.
